title: Latency-aware schema assertor for constrained decoding in streaming responses
creator: Priya Patel
description: Implement and validate a schema assertion layer (assertor) that enforces JSON-mode / constrained-decoding contracts on streaming outputs without violating client-perceived latency SLOs. The assertor must work with partial emissions, allow graceful degradation (repair heuristics / fallbacks), and expose telemetry to quantify cost vs correctness trade-offs.
motivation: Existing schema gates and strict decoders reduce malformed structured outputs but can add blocking points in the streaming path or cause high token-level retries. We need an assertor that enforces schema adherence early while keeping tail latency within customer SLOs and providing robust fallback policies for production use (canary first).
technical_approach: 1) Build a non-blocking 'assertor' component that runs incrementally on token streams. 2) Detect schema deviations using lightweight sentinel heuristics and a partial-JSON incremental parser. 3) If deviation is reparable within a small budget (token/backtrack budget), emit a repair patch and continue streaming. 4) If not reparable or repair would exceed latency budget, trigger configurable fallback (best-effort JSON envelope + telemetry + post-hoc repair async job). 5) Integrate with existing constrained-decoder interface so decoder sampling policies can be adjusted based on assertor feedback (soft gating).
implementation_details:
- Language: Rust core for the assertor (same runtime binary as streaming gateway) with a thin Go shim for platform config.
- Incremental parser: optimized, allocation-light parser that accepts partial objects and returns deterministic repair suggestions.
- Latency budget: per-request token latency budget configurable per route (default p90 <= 120ms). Assertor must early-exit if cumulative decode time exceeds 30% of token budget.
- Signals: sentinel tokens, escape markers, and a compact binary flag to mark repaired spans in streaming events.
- Config: route-level toggles (enforce|observe|best-effort), repair aggressiveness (strict|moderate|lenient), and fallbacks (sync-fallback vs. async-postprocess).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for incremental parser on partial streams and corner cases (unterminated arrays, truncated strings, interleaved toolcall tokens).
- Microbenchmarks: decode+assertor p50/p90/p99 for different model sizes and token lengths.
- Integration tests: end-to-end streaming with constrained decoder enabled and with simulated toolcall interleaves.
- Chaos tests: inject high-latency asserts to validate assertor early-exit and fallback behavior.
- Backcompat: run existing structured-output regression suite (select subset of ENG-... guardrail tests) to validate no regressions in normal mode.
- Canary: run on 1% traffic for two routes, compare schema failure and latency metrics against baseline for 48 hours.
acceptance_criteria:
- Assertor has feature flags and can be toggled per-route.
- Microbenchmarks show p90 token additional overhead <= 20ms on standard routes under default configuration.
- Canary (1% traffic) shows schema failure rate reduced by >= 70% vs baseline when enforce mode is on, with streaming p99 increase < 10% above baseline.
- Telemetry surfaces a clear set of metrics (schema_failure_rate, repaired_emits, fallback_rate, assertor_cpu_ms_per_token, assertor_block_exits).
- Documentation and runbook added to Console and runbooks: how to choose repair aggressiveness, how to interpret telemetry, and how to roll back.
- Unit and integration tests included, and a PR with CI passing.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flags behind route-level config. 2) Internal dogfood for 2 weeks on non-critical models. 3) Canary on 1% of production traffic for 48h; monitor telemetry and error budgets. 4) Increase to 10% and run for 1 week. 5) Gradual ramp with automated rollback if fallback_rate or latency SLOs breached. 6) Post-rollout: schedule follow-up observation window (2 weeks) before enabling enforce mode for all routes.
risks:
- Assertor could add unexpected CPU cost under high QPS leading to infra pressure.
- Repair heuristics might mask upstream model regression, causing silent correctness regressions.
- Interactions with toolcall interleaving could cause false positives; careful testing required.
- Complexity in code path increases maintenance burden.
follow_up_tasks:
- (post-launch) collect corpus of repaired payloads and run classifier to prioritize model-owner fixes.
- Add opt-in sample export to customer S3 for high-severity repair events.
- Iterate repair heuristics based on corpus.
- Explore moving hot-path to an assembly-optimized decode kernel if assertor CPU dominates.
- Product: add console toggle and visualization for repaired spans.
notes:
- Coordinate with SDK team for sentinel flag semantics in streaming SDKs.
- Coordinate with privacy/compliance to ensure repaired payload storage meets retention rules.
- Discuss whether repair markers should be included in response by default or behind an audit header.
- Schedule architecture review with runtime and infra leads (Ava Chen, David Kim).
